final.summary: The ETP stopped between 12:05 and 16:05 on 13 October, with power at standby and no flow through the ETP or outfall during that stretch. Outside the stop, power matched the load expected for its inflow and outfall pH stayed near neutral. The equalization tank level is missing over the stop, so it cannot be shown that arriving wastewater was held in the tank.

explanations.label: ETP stopped 12:05-16:05 but wastewater held in equalization tank
Aeration cut / power cut with flow continuing

key_evidence.why: Power matched expected load across treatment interval, showing aeration ran when flowing.
Power feed not replayed, so power evidence can be relied on.
Outfall pH stayed near neutral with no excursion above 9, showing no raw wastewater reached outfall.
Power at standby level confirms ETP was stopped as claimed.
ETP inflow zero during stop shows no flow went through ETP then.
Outfall flow zero during stop shows nothing passed the outfall meter then.
Meter photo agrees with feed, confirming standby power was real.
Tank balance cannot be computed without T1, so holding cannot be verified.

final.scope_line: Based on flow, power, pH and conductivity records for 2026-10-13 10:00 to 2026-10-14 14:00. Does not measure every pollutant.
limitations: Equalization tank level T1 has no coverage over the treatment interval, so the tank balance cannot be computed and the rise of the tank cannot be checked against arriving volume.

ETP inflow and outfall flow were flat at zero during the stop; a stuck meter cannot be ruled out on its own, but power standby and neutral pH provide separate signals that the stop was real and no raw water reached the outfall.
Lab sample at 13:20 was taken while outfall flow was zero, so it does not represent discharged effluent from that time.
Conductivity and full outfall flow series for the remainder of the treatment interval were not examined within the check budget.
Factory logbook and maintenance record are claims, not facts; the stop timing was tested against signals.

evidence_request.reason: A rising tank level with ETP at standby and zero outfall flow would show arriving water was held; without it the stop cannot be assessed.

result.note: ETP balance: treated flow reaching the outfall vs outfall flow (same time). Boundary balance: intake vs outfall + losses + sludge water + tank storage change (reuse cancels). Tank balance: wastewater arriving (estimated from intake) vs ETP inflow + storage change; unaccounted water left the tank another way, or was intake water that never became wastewater. null means a required signal is under 80% coverage.
